reasons: Tests the main integrity rules directly against a real database.
Checks both database rules and input validation.
Clear expected error messages for refused changes.

terms.meaning: The structure of the database: which tables and columns exist and what they hold.
Records can be added but not changed or deleted. Corrections are new records.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sets up test competition and event
sections.what: Resets the test database and creates a competition, season and event so incidents have somewhere to belong.
sections.why: Likely reason: incidents must link to an event, so each test run needs one set up first.
sections.watch_out: The event is created once and shared by all tests, so a test that changes it affects later tests.

sections.name: base
sections.title: Shared valid incident template
sections.what: Defines one valid ball record with timestamps, source and rights, which each test copies and changes slightly.
sections.why: Likely reason: copying one valid example keeps tests short and ensures they only change one thing at a time.
sections.watch_out: Changing these values changes several tests at once, so change them with care.

sections.name: multi-sport domain schema
sections.title: Checks schema rules
sections.what: Checks five sports are seeded, incidents keep both clocks, source and rights, updates and deletes are refused, corrections link to originals, duplicate source records are refused, and adapter input is checked at the boundary.
sections.why: Likely reason: these rules keep the stored history reliable and auditable.
sections.watch_out: Refusals come from the database itself. If a migration removes those rules, these tests will fail, which is the intended warning.

summary: Tests the database schema for the multi-sport fact store: sports are seeded, incidents keep both timestamps and rights, records cannot be edited or deleted, and corrections point back to the original.
purpose: Protects the integrity of stored match facts, so that the record of what happened can be trusted and audited.
why: Likely reason: an append-only record means history cannot be quietly rewritten, which matters for fan calls and grading.
how: Before the tests, resets the database and creates a competition, season and event. Then checks that five sports are seeded, that an incident stores both clocks, source and rights, that updates and deletes are refused, that corrections link to the original, that duplicate source records are refused, and that adapter input is validated.
inputs: A shared valid incident template, plus the database and the sport list from the types module.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The tests write to the test database.
risks: The append-only rule depends on the database layer. Removing it would break these tests, which is the intent. Shared setup means one failed write can affect later tests.
debug: If a test fails, check the database schema and the migration that created it. For append-only failures, check the database rules on the incident table.
